newsitem.title: CHINA: China auto prices seen still falling in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China auto prices seen still falling in 1997.

text.p: China's automobile prices are expected to continue to slide in 1997 because of rapidly growing domestic stockpiles, the Beijing Economic Daily said on Monday.
China had stockpiles of 101,300 vehicles at the end of September, up 33.5 percent compared with the same period last year, the newspaper said.
Stockpiles were expected to hit a record 200,000 vehicles by the end of this year, the newspaper said. Automakers have cut their prices this year to try to revive flagging sales.
"Experts predict that in order to stimulate consumption, the prices of automobiles will continue to fall," it said.
Sluggish domestic demand and protectionist regional policies fuelled the expansion of stockpiles, it said.

China produced 992,000 automobiles in January-September, just 64 percent of expected output for the whole year, while sales in the period rose 0.63 percent to 960,400 units, it said. It gave no further details.
